$comment: Handwritten help text for every public import and export option, keyed by public name. It is the only source of option prose; nothing is read from the engine headers. A null entry ships the option without a description because its name says everything. An export entry is one text for every target that exposes the option, or an object keyed by target where "*" covers the remaining targets. Families expand per import format. The generator fails on a missing or unknown entry and on prose that breaks its style checks. Kind, default, range and allowed values are registry data, so prose does not repeat them.

families.UnitScaleToMeters: Length of one {format} file unit in meters, for example 0.001 for millimeters. Exports convert from it to the target format's unit.
families.UpAxis: Axis that points up in {format} files. Exports rotate the model from it to the target format's up axis.

import.appScaleKey: Has no effect: every import replaces it with the file's own unit scale. Use globalScaleFactorKey to scale the scene.
import.favourSpeed: Trade accuracy for speed where an importer or post-process step has a faster path, such as findInstances skipping its bone and face comparisons and LightWave objects skipping smoothing-angle normals.
import.fbxConvertToM: Has no effect. FBX files are converted from centimeters to meters only by the globalScale post-process step.
import.fbxUseSkeletonBoneContainer: Store FBX skin weights in a separate skeleton instead of as bones on each mesh. No exporter reads that skeleton, so exports lose the skinning. Experimental.
import.globalScaleFactorKey: Uniform scale applied to the whole scene, including animation. Used by the globalScale post-process step, which also applies FBX unit conversion.
import.globMeasureTime: Log how long each import phase takes. The log is discarded, so this has no visible effect; every result reports timings anyway.
import.importAcEvalSubdivision: Subdivide AC3D surfaces that declare a subdivision level, using Catmull-Clark. Off, the coarse control mesh is imported.
import.importAcSeparateBfcull: Put AC3D surfaces that have the backface-culling flag into separate meshes from the rest.
import.importAseReconstructNormals: Rebuild ASE normals from the file's smoothing groups instead of using the stored normals, which are often invalid.
import.importColladaIgnoreUnitSize: Ignore the unit declared in the COLLADA header and keep coordinates as stored.
import.importColladaIgnoreUpDirection: Ignore the up axis declared in the COLLADA header and keep the scene as stored.
import.importColladaUseColladaNames: Name nodes and meshes after their COLLADA name attribute instead of their id, or their sid when there is no id.
import.importFbxEmbeddedTexturesLegacyNaming: Reference embedded FBX textures by index, such as *0, instead of by file name.
import.importFbxIgnoreUpDirection: Ignore the axes declared in the FBX file and keep the scene as stored, without rotating it.
import.importFbxOptimizeEmptyAnimationCurves: Drop FBX animation curves that are empty or match the bind pose over their whole range.
import.importFbxPreservePivots: Keep FBX pivot and offset transforms as extra helper nodes. Off, they are folded into each node's transform where possible.
import.importFbxReadAllGeometryLayers: Merge every geometry layer in an FBX file. Off, only the first layer is read.
import.importFbxReadAllMaterials: Import every FBX material, including ones no mesh uses.
import.importFbxReadWeights: Import the skin weights that bind FBX meshes to bones.
import.importFbxStrictMode: Reject FBX files newer than version 7.4 and fail on a malformed object instead of skipping it with a warning.
import.importGlobalKeyframe: Frame to import from animated MD2, MD3, MDC, MDL, SMD and Unreal models, counting from 0, since only one frame is kept. Each format's own keyframe option overrides it.
import.importLwoLayerIndex: Import only the LightWave layer at this position, counting from 1. The import fails when there is no such layer.
import.importLwoLayerName: Import only the LightWave layer with this name. The import fails when no layer has it.
import.importLwsAnimEnd: Last frame of the LightWave scene animation to import, counting from 0. The default keeps the end the file declares.
import.importLwsAnimStart: First frame of the LightWave scene animation to import, counting from 0. The default keeps the start the file declares.
import.importMd2Keyframe: Frame to import from an animated MD2 model, counting from 0. -1 uses importGlobalKeyframe.
import.importMd3HandleMultipart: Load the lower, upper and head parts of a Quake 3 player model together when one of them is imported.
import.importMd3Keyframe: Frame to import from an animated MD3 model, counting from 0. -1 uses importGlobalKeyframe.
import.importMd3LoadShaders: Read Quake 3 shader files to resolve MD3 texture paths. Off, texture paths are used as stored.
import.importMd3ShaderSrc: Quake 3 shader file for MD3 materials, or a directory that holds a shader file named after the model. Empty searches the scripts directory three levels above the model.
import.importMd3SkinName: Skin to apply to MD3 models, such as red or blue, read from the model's matching .skin file.
import.importMd5NoAnimAutoload: Skip loading the MD5ANIM file that shares an MD5MESH file's name and directory.
import.importMdcKeyframe: Frame to import from an animated MDC model, counting from 0. -1 uses importGlobalKeyframe.
import.importMdlColormap: Palette file for textures embedded in Quake 1 and 3D GameStudio MDL files: 256 RGB triplets in 768 bytes. When it is missing, the Quake 1 palette is used.
import.importMdlHl1ReadAnimationEvents: Import animation events of Half-Life models. Needs importMdlHl1ReadAnimations.
import.importMdlHl1ReadBlendControllers: Import blend controllers of Half-Life models. Needs importMdlHl1ReadAnimations.
import.importMdlHl1ReadMiscGlobalInfo: Import a Half-Life model's eye position and its hull and collision bounds as scene metadata.
import.importMdlHl1ReadSequenceTransitions: Import the sequence transition graph of Half-Life models. Needs importMdlHl1ReadAnimations.
import.importMdlHl1TransformCoordSystem: Rotate Half-Life models about the Z and X axes into the Y-up frame. Off, they get the single 90-degree X rotation used for other MDL files.
import.importMdlKeyframe: Frame to import from an animated MDL model, counting from 0. -1 uses importGlobalKeyframe.
import.importNoSkeletonMeshes: Skip the placeholder mesh built from the skeleton when a file has bones but no geometry, such as a BVH motion file.
import.importOgreMaterialFile: Material file to search last when an Ogre material is in neither its own .material file nor the one named after the mesh.
import.importOgreTexturetypeFromFilename: Infer Ogre texture roles from file name suffixes: _n or _normal for normal maps, _s or _spec for specular, _l or _occ for light maps, and _disp for displacement.
import.importRemoveEmptyBones: Remove bones that influence no vertex. Applies to COLLADA files and the limitBoneWeights post-process step; turn off to keep bones that only mark attachment points.
import.importSmdKeyframe: Frame to import from an animated SMD model, counting from 0. -1 uses importGlobalKeyframe.
import.importSmdLoadAnimationList: Also load the animations listed in the _animation.txt file named after an SMD model.
import.importUnrealHandleFlags: Put Unreal faces with different surface flags, such as two-sided and one-sided, into separate meshes.
import.importUnrealKeyframe: Frame to import from an animated Unreal model, counting from 0. -1 uses importGlobalKeyframe.
import.importUsdMaxMemoryMb: Memory budget, in MiB, for reading one USD file and every layer it composes. Raise it for very large scenes; lower it to reject oversized files early.
import.pointClouds: Has no effect on import; set the export option of the same name to keep point clouds.
import.ppCtMaxSmoothingAngle: Largest angle, in degrees, between tangents that are still smoothed together, up to 45. Used by the calcTangentSpace post-process step.
import.ppCtTextureChannelIndex: Texture coordinate set that tangents are derived from, counting from 0. Used by the calcTangentSpace post-process step.
import.ppDbAllOrNone: Remove bones only when every bone in a mesh can go, otherwise keep them all. Used by the debone post-process step.
import.ppDbThreshold: Smallest weight at which a vertex counts as rigidly bound to one bone; lower it to remove more bones. Used by the debone post-process step.
import.ppFdCheckarea: Also treat triangles with almost no area as degenerate. Used by the findDegenerates post-process step.
import.ppFdRemove: Delete degenerate faces instead of turning them into lines and points. Used by the findDegenerates post-process step.
import.ppFidAnimAccuracy: Tolerance for treating animation keys as equal when dropping tracks that never change. 0 compares exactly, and any larger value acts as a tolerance of 1. Used by the findInvalidData post-process step.
import.ppFidIgnoreTexturecoords: Skip the texture coordinate check, which removes coordinate sets that are all equal or hold invalid numbers. Used by the findInvalidData post-process step.
import.ppGsnMaxSmoothingAngle: Largest angle, in degrees, between face normals that are still smoothed together, up to 175; sharper edges get a hard seam. Used by the generateSmoothNormals post-process step.
import.ppIclPtcacheSize: Vertex cache size, in vertices, that triangles are reordered for. Used by the improveCacheLocality post-process step.
import.ppLbwMaxWeights: Most bones that may influence one vertex; the weakest extra weights are dropped and the rest renormalized. Used by the limitBoneWeights post-process step.
import.ppOgExcludeList: Node names to keep unchanged, separated by spaces; wrap a name that contains spaces in single quotes. Used by the optimizeGraph post-process step.
import.ppPtvAddRootTransformation: Apply ppPtvRootTransformation to the scene root before transforms are baked. Used by the preTransformVertices post-process step.
import.ppPtvKeepHierarchy: Keep the node hierarchy: meshes move to world space but are not merged. Used by the preTransformVertices post-process step.
import.ppPtvNormalize: Scale the scene uniformly to fit the -1 to 1 range. Used by the preTransformVertices post-process step.
import.ppPtvRootTransformation: Root transform applied when ppPtvAddRootTransformation is on, as 16 numbers in row-major order. Used by the preTransformVertices post-process step.
import.ppRrmExcludeList: Material names to keep even when they duplicate another material, separated by spaces; wrap a name that contains spaces in single quotes. Used by the removeRedundantMaterials post-process step.
import.ppRvcFlags: Components to remove, as a sum of flags: 2 normals, 4 tangents, 8 colors, 16 texture coordinates, 32 bone weights, 64 animations, 128 textures, 256 lights, 512 cameras, 1024 meshes, 2048 materials. Used by the removeComponent post-process step.
import.ppSbbcMaxBones: Most bones one mesh may use before it is split. Used by the splitByBoneCount post-process step.
import.ppSbpRemove: Primitive types to remove, as a sum of flags: 1 points, 2 lines, 4 triangles, 8 polygons. Used by the sortByPrimitiveType post-process step.
import.ppSlmTriangleLimit: Most triangles one mesh may have before it is split. Used by the splitLargeMeshes post-process step, and optimizeMeshes stays below it when merging.
import.ppSlmVertexLimit: Most vertices one mesh may have before it is split. Used by the splitLargeMeshes post-process step, and optimizeMeshes stays below it when merging.
import.ppTuvEvaluate: Texture transforms to bake into texture coordinates, as a sum of flags: 1 scaling, 2 rotation, 4 translation. Used by the transformUvCoords post-process step.

export.animationIndex: Animation to export, counting from 0, when several animations drive the same nodes. USD has one timeline, so animations on separate nodes are merged and this is ignored.
export.application: Application name written to the file's metadata. Empty writes none.
export.clearcoat: Write material clearcoat strength and roughness, including their textures.
export.compressFloatArrays: Losslessly compress float arrays that hold whole numbers or few distinct values, which makes the USDC data smaller.
export.decimalPrecision: Digits written after the decimal point for each coordinate. Fewer digits make a smaller file but can open hairline gaps between objects in slicers.
export.identityMatrixEpsilon: Tolerance within which a node transform counts as identity and is left out of the file.
export.includeTargetNames: Write morph target names to each mesh's extras.targetNames.
export.includeTargetNormals: Write normals for morph targets as well as positions.
export.joinIdenticalVertices: Write identical vertices once and share them between faces. Off, every face corner gets its own vertex, which makes a larger file.
export.lights: Keep lights in the package. ARKit's USDZ profile forbids them, so they are dropped by default.
export.materials: Write materials to an MTL file next to the OBJ. Off, the OBJ holds geometry only.

maxFileSizeMb.usda: Has no effect on USDA, which is written as text without a size limit.
maxFileSizeMb.usdc: Largest file the export may write, in MiB; a larger scene fails. 0 uses 2048 MiB in WebAssembly and no limit natively.
maxFileSizeMb.usdz: Largest USDC layer the package may hold, in MiB; a larger scene fails. 0 uses 2048 MiB in WebAssembly and no limit natively.

maxMemoryMb.usda: Has no effect on USDA, which is written as text without a memory limit.
maxMemoryMb.usdc: Memory the USDC writer may use, in MiB; a larger scene fails. 0 uses 2048 MiB in WebAssembly and no limit natively.
maxMemoryMb.usdz: Memory the USDC writer may use, in MiB; a larger scene fails. 0 uses 2048 MiB in WebAssembly and no limit natively.

export.physicsJoints: Keep physics joints in the package. ARKit's USDZ profile forbids them, so by default joint nodes are written as plain transforms.

pointClouds.*: Has no effect on this format; only PLY export uses it.
pointClouds.ply: Keep vertices that no face uses, such as a point cloud. Node transforms are then not baked into the written vertices.

export.requireManifold: Fail the export when a mesh is not closed and consistently oriented, as 3MF requires for printable objects. Off, such a mesh is written as an object of type other instead.
export.skipWhitespaces: Write compact JSON without indentation or line breaks.
export.sparseAccessors: Store morph target data in sparse accessors, which keeps files small when a target moves few vertices.
export.transparencyFactorRefersToOpacity: Write each material's TransparencyFactor as 1 minus its opacity. Off, it is written as 1 and readers such as Maya and Blender take transparency from the Opacity property.
export.unit: Unit the file declares. Geometry is rescaled into it when the source unit is known; otherwise coordinates are written unchanged.
export.unlimitedSkinningBonesPerVertex: Write every bone influence per vertex in extra JOINTS and WEIGHTS sets. Off, only the four strongest are kept, the limit every glTF viewer supports.
export.upAxis: Axis that points up in the file. The model is rotated into it when the source up axis is known.
export.useGltfPbrSpecularGlossiness: Write specular materials with the deprecated KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness extension instead of KHR_materials_specular. Those materials then also lose sheen, clearcoat and other material extensions.
